title: Thirty-one years, 27 moments
lede: From a student project to a shell company that still files quarterly reports. Filter by thread.

events.title: Incorporated
events.text: Todd V. Krizelman and Stephan J. Paternot found the company; it is incorporated on May 1, 1995.

events.title: The chairman’s agreement
events.text: Michael Egan, his company Dancing Bear Investments, the two founders and two directors sign a stockholders’ agreement on board nominees.

events.title: Offering cut
events.text: The planned range of $11 to $13 a share is cut to $8 to $10.

events.title: Offering shelved
events.text: The company postpones the IPO because of weak demand.

events.title: Priced at $9
events.text: 3.1 million shares are priced at $9, raising $27.9M.

events.title: A record first day
events.text: The stock opens at $67, touches $97 and closes at $63.50, up 606%, a record first-day gain.

events.title: An online store
events.text: Buys factorymall.com (Azazz.com) for $22.8M and turns it into shop.theglobe.com.

events.title: Games sites from Britain
events.text: Buys Attitude Network, owner of Games Domain, Kids Domain and Console Domain, for $46.8M.

events.title: Stock split
events.text: A two-for-one stock split. Later price tables are adjusted for it.

events.title: $65M more
events.text: A follow-on offering sells 3.5 million new shares at $20.00, for net proceeds of $65.0M.

events.title: Web hosting
events.text: Buys the web-hosting assets of Webjump for $13.0M, mostly in shares.

events.title: 220 employees
events.text: The year ends with about 220 full-time staff, 4.7 million unique users and 3.6 million registered members.

events.title: Games magazine
events.text: Buys Chips & Bits and Strategy Plus, publisher of Computer Games magazine, for about $15.3M.

events.title: A new chief executive
events.text: Charles Peck becomes chief executive, replacing the founders.

events.title: The $103.9M year
events.text: Revenue peaks at $29.9M; the net loss is $103.9M, including $41.3M of restructuring and impairment charges.

events.title: Delisted
events.text: Nasdaq delists the stock; it moves to the over-the-counter bulletin board.

events.title: Closure announced
events.text: The company says it will close the community and Webjump and cut 60 jobs, 49% of staff.

events.title: The site goes dark
events.text: The community at www.theglobe.com closes.

events.title: Games sites sold
events.text: Games Domain and Console Domain go to British Telecommunications, Kids Domain to Kaboose.

events.title: Happy Puppy sold
events.text: The Happy Puppy games site is sold to Internet Game Distribution.

events.title: Egan takes over
events.text: Chairman Michael Egan becomes chief executive. By December the company has about 21 employees.

events.title: Internet phones
events.text: The company buys voice-over-IP assets for warrants.

events.title: .travel
events.text: Acquires Tralliance, the registry for the .travel domain.

events.title: Games and phones shut
events.text: Management decides to shut the computer games and telephony businesses.

events.title: A shell
events.text: Tralliance is sold to a company controlled by Egan, which also receives 229 million new shares. theglobe.com has no operating business left.

events.title: New controlling owner
events.text: Egan and his companies agree to sell 70.9% of the shares to Delfin Midstream.

events.title: Still filing
events.text: The shell files its 2025 annual report. It has no employees, and its liabilities exceed its assets.
